rationale: Excluding object and function before String leaves exactly standard primitive categories in Node. Primitive helper returns null for null/objects/functions as before. Outer Error.message and null string handling remain unchanged. String(primitive string) returns same string; explicit String(symbol) supported and matches previous positive guard. Numeric,BigInt,boolean andundefined behavior retained. Actual TS checker type at String call is recorded rather than inferred from syntax alone.
limits: No source edit or scanner disposition.
No new DeepSource/Sonar scan passed. TypeScript still displays {} | undefined; static scanner acceptance remains unverified.
Global built-ins assumed unmodified. If String is monkeypatched, new string case invokes it where old direct string return did not; production uses standard global String.
Host exotic document.all does not exist in Node22; not a browser-host-exotic equivalence claim.
Error subclasses or hostile proxies may trigger preexisting outer instanceof/message side effects; unchanged outer operations are not newly hardened.
typescriptFinding: Actual TypeScript6.0.3 strict checker leaves {} | undefined at String(error), not explicit string|number|bigint|boolean|symbol|undefined. Runtime exclusion is exhaustive in Node but this is not static proof that SonarS6551 will disappear. Fresh scanner needed or a different explicit type guard if scanner still flags it.
